items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: you'll hear (inaudible) do that. So he was behind Paul Gonzalez (inaudible)

ctx.x: Because he wanted to go home. See, he didn't want to do anything I wouldn't like. I said, 'Well, so man, you got one chord, doesn't mean you play one chord with the same voicing every time. I said, 'Use the passing chords.' He was (inaudible) said, 'Why don't you write it out for me?' I said, 'It will take you years to write that out.' I said, at Duke; 'Look, when he plays the blues, he plays a different set on every chord change -- on every blues sequence.' He said, 'I haven't heard Duke "" you listen Gonzales,…
Oh, was it pianos? as a pianist? Yes, I agree with that.
